method: Five-fold shuffled engine-level cross-validation of threshold selection using existing validation predictions. Thresholds are selected within each policy-training fold and evaluated on its held-out engines. Final thresholds are selected using all validation engines and then evaluated on test engines.
limitations: Only 20 validation engines are available in the current FD001 prediction file, so five-fold estimates will have high uncertainty.
This cross-validation assesses threshold-selection stability using existing predictions. It does not retrain the RUL prediction models in each fold.
The final test set is not used for threshold selection.
Cost values and safety boundaries are illustrative research assumptions, not validated industrial costs.
A feasible policy on a small validation fold does not establish real-world safety.
The policy is a threshold rule, not reinforcement learning or proof of self-evolving behavior.
